key_insight: A PDE-consistent deep neural network closure, trained jointly with the LES solver, can replace a standard eddy-viscosity model and better capture heat-release-driven turbulence modulation in premixed jet flames.
engineering_relevance: This offers a more accurate and generalizable turbulence model for large-eddy simulation of reacting flows, with potential impact on predictive combustion design and reduced model-form error across operating regimes.
method: Augmented eddy-viscosity closure built with deep neural networks
Solver-in-the-loop training using adjoint-based optimization and differentiable programming
Evaluated for interpolation and extrapolation across Damköhler-number regimes
evidence_signal: Compared with the Smagorinsky baseline, the best model reduced a posteriori LES errors by 25-50% for primitive variables and by more than 60% for resolved Reynolds stress and scalar flux, while remaining stable out of sample.
watch_item: The approach depends on careful solver–network coupling and training objective design, so robustness and cost may vary when transferred to different flames, grids, or combustion regimes.
paper_title: Solver-in-the-loop training of deep learning closures for large-eddy simulation of turbulent premixed jet flames
